summary.answer: Source-visible answer: the exclusion/placeholder primitive and the duplicate-registration enabler. ignore(str_name): asserts level.gametype is UNdefined (must run before the engine assigns the gametype - pre-gametype window only); then if no registry record exists, register(name, undefined, undefined, undefined) creates an all-undefined placeholder; finally sets .ignore=1 (169-179). Combined with register()'s duplicate rule (assert existing .ignore then return, 11-15) this yields the exact wz/HMH exclusion semantics: a system whose name is pre-ignored either (a) never stores its real pre/post functions - the later real register returns early, or (b) if real registration happened first, ignore skips placeholder creation and sets the existing record.ignore=1 while preserving its pointers; ignore asserts only that level.gametype is undefined (171), and register has the separate duplicate as [excerpt; exact source record identified separately]
summary.behavior: ignore(str_name): assert(!isdefined(level.gametype), devx124) (171) - the assert boundary records that exclusions are only valid while no gametype is set; if !level.system_funcs or the name is unregistered, register(str_name, undefined, undefined, undefined) creates a placeholder with undefined pre/post funcs and predone=postdone=1 (both !isdefined) (173-176); then level.system_funcs[str_name].ignore = 1 (178). Consequences: (1) an undefined-func placeholder would never invoke anything even without ignore (exec_* call [[undefined]] guarded by predone/postdone=1 and ignore skip); (2) later register() by the real system hits the early return (11-15, assert passes because ignore=1) so its pointers are discarded; (3) exec pre/post paths skip the record regardless (37-40/102-105). The wz ignore_systems autoexec runs in both server (wz_ignore_systems.gsc) and client (wz_ignore_systems.csc) VMs [excerpt; exact source record identified separately]
